strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas-to_datetime accuracy regression (GH#60506 / PR#60510) where DataFrame float32 components produce incorrect timestamps vs the float64 path. The failing transition is the addition of a regression test that asserts exact Series equality for a float32-cast DataFrame; it fails on buggy commit b667fdf8dd4e and passes after the fix that coerces float inputs to float64 in `coerce(values)`.

pinned_because: numpy is numerically relevant and must be 2.1.2 as per provided environment evidence
Python is 3.12.7 as per provided environment evidence

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision b667fdf8dd4e, `test_dataframe_float32_dtype` fails because `to_datetime(df.astype(np.float32), cache=cache)` returns a Series that is not exactly equal to the expected two `Timestamp(...)` values; on fixed revision (PR#60510 merged / commit containing float->float64 coercion in `pandas/core/tools/datetimes.py::coerce`), the same assertion passes (exact `tm.assert_series_equal`).
strategy.numerical_probe: The test checks exact equality of the resulting Series to fixed `Timestamp("20150204 06:58:10.001002003")` and `Timestamp("20160305 07:59:11.001002003")` after casting the input DataFrame to float32 before calling `to_datetime(..., cache=cache)`.

input_output_examples.input: DataFrame with columns including year/month/day/hour/minute/second (provided by the fixture `df` used by this test), cast with `df.astype(np.float32)` then passed to `to_datetime`.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: unknown (not provided in supplied passage); test fails on buggy revision due to mismatch with expected timestamps.

risks: This strategy assumes the failure is reproducible with the provided toolchain (Python 3.12.7, numpy 2.1.2). If the bug is sensitive to a different numpy build/BLAS or CPU architecture, it may not transition.

The evidence does not specify the exact contents of the `df` fixture used by `test_dataframe_float32_dtype`; the test relies on pandas’ existing fixture setup. The transition is still valid because it is the project’s own regression assertion.

If the fix is already present in the checked-out pandas revision (e.g., if running against a post-PR build), the buggy failure will not occur; you must check out specifically b667fdf8dd4e (buggy) and the fixed commit/merge result for the passing run.

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/tools/test_to_datetime.py regression expectation for GH#60506; exact Series equality via `tm.assert_series_equal` to the two specified `Timestamp(...)` values
oracle.why: The added regression test asserts exact equality of the full resulting Series, not a tolerance-based numeric metric.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: `tm.assert_series_equal(result, expected)` fails because `to_datetime(df.astype(np.float32), cache=cache)` produces incorrect timestamps (float32 precision not handled), causing at least one element (or dtype/metadata) in the resulting Series to differ from the expected exact timestamps.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: `tm.assert_series_equal(result, expected)` passes after the fix in `pandas/core/tools/datetimes.py::coerce(values)` that coerces float dtype inputs to float64 (preventing float32 precision issues as noted in the PR diff comment for GH#60506).
